item.title: XSS: Going Deeper
item.description:
Most people learn XSS as <script>alert(1)</script> and stop there. The interesting part starts once that stops working.

Contexts matter

Where your input lands changes everything: HTML body, an attribute, a JS string, a URL. Each context has its own escape sequence, and filters are usually built for one context while your input lands in another.

Bypassing filters

Filters that strip <script> tags rarely catch event handlers, javascript: URIs, or encoded payloads. This is less about clever tricks and more about understanding what the filter actually checks versus what the browser actually parses.
